title: The integral bar resolution and its cochain complex
statement:
Let $G$ be a group and let $R=\mathbf Z[G]$ be its integral group ring. For $n\geq0$ let $B_n(G)$ be the free left $R$-module with basis $[g_1|\cdots|g_n]$ indexed by $G^n$ (the empty tuple gives the basis element $[\ ]$ of $B_0(G)=R$). For $n\geq1$ prescribe the $R$-linear differential by
$$d_n[g_1|\cdots|g_n]=g_1[g_2|\cdots|g_n]+\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}(-1)^j[g_1|\cdots|g_jg_{j+1}|\cdots|g_n]+(-1)^n[g_1|\cdots|g_{n-1}].$$
Let $\epsilon_B:B_0(G)\to\mathbf Z$ send $\sum_g a_g g[\ ]$ to $\sum_g a_g$, where $\mathbf Z$ has trivial $G$-action. These data form an exact augmented nonnegative chain complex [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology] (augmented exactness means that $\epsilon_B$ is surjective, $\ker\epsilon_B=\operatorname{im}d_1$, and $\ker d_n=\operatorname{im}d_{n+1}$ for $n\geq1$) whose terms are projective: every $R$-linear map from $B_n(G)$ lifts through every surjective $R$-linear map. For any abelian group $M$ with $G$-action by automorphisms, the assignment $a\mapsto((g_1,\ldots,g_n)\mapsto a([g_1|\cdots|g_n]))$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_R(B_\bullet(G),M)$, with differential $a\mapsto a\circ d$, with the complex of all functions $G^n\to M$ and differential
$$(\delta c)(g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})=g_1c(g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1})+\sum_{j=1}^{n}(-1)^jc(g_1,\ldots,g_jg_{j+1},\ldots,g_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}c(g_1,\ldots,g_n).$$
